periods.analysis: Winter is the slow season for fresh produce, and only 140 households used matching dollars at the indoor market. Nutrition and cooking sessions still reached 160 residents, mostly at library branches, and garden sites in Riverside and East Flats were approved for the coming season.
periods.recommendations: Open the outdoor market with weekly matching dollars and add cooking demonstrations at school family nights.

periods.analysis: Matching dollar use nearly tripled to 410 households once the outdoor market opened in May, and nutrition sessions reached 245 residents. Beds at the two new garden plots are prepared for summer planting.
periods.recommendations: Plant the new gardens, add a farm stand at the Bayfront library, and launch a sugary-drink campaign for back-to-school.

periods.analysis: Summer was the strongest stretch for produce access, with garden harvests, farm stands and matching-dollar markets all operating at full capacity. Nutrition education is reaching families through schools, libraries and neighborhood events. The challenge now is carrying that momentum through the winter months when outdoor sites close.
periods.recommendations: Move the matching-dollar program indoors for winter and expand cooking demonstrations.
